title: SSE rate-surge debug journal
content:
Context:
- Observed intermittent client disconnects and partial frames during sustained short bursts (rate surges) to the hosted API streaming endpoint (/v1/generate).
- Repro triggers when many short requests (prompt length <= 30 tokens) are sent with high ramp QPS and small client read window; effects not seen for long-running single requests.
- Hypothesis: batching + continuous KV cache + runtime backpressure interplay is dropping or coalescing chunk frames when burst causes internal queue oscillation.

Env and quick facts:
- cluster: prod-dedicated-us-west-2 (dedicated pool of g4dn-like nodes)
- runtime: 1.18.3 (serving runtime), kernel-selection enabled, continuous-batching on
- models: rw-medium-v2 (causal lm), seq-len typical 32
- client: node 20 (fetch SSE polyfill), python requests for head checks, k6/wrk2 for load generation

Observed behavior summary:
- Clients see: first few events OK, then a sequence of tiny chunks ("\n" only) or a stuck connection (no more data) followed by a truncated final JSON when connection closed.
- Server logs: no hard OOM, but there are spikes in "request-queue-length" and "batch-formation-time"; worker thread reports occasional "stall detected" traces.
- tcpdump (server egress) shows TCP packets with empty payloads / FINs after stall.

Repro commands tried (ordered, with notes):
1) Simple curl SSE test (baseline)
- curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=rw-medium-v2" \n  -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":20}'
- Notes: Stable, produces stream as expected for single client.

2) wrk2 microburst pattern (repro of short-burst QPS)
- wrk2 -t10 -c200 -d30s -R1000 --latency -s scripts/sse_wrk.lua https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
- sse_wrk.lua uses short POST bodies and reads until connection close.
- Notes: After 10s, ~4% of connections show partial frames; server trace shows increased "batch-formation-time" for the short requests.

3) k6 with ramping arrival rate, short-lived connections
- k6 script: stages ramp to 1200 RPS over 20s, each VU sends POST, reads SSE for 200ms then closes.
- Observed more frequent partial frames and SSE clients reporting EPIPE.

4) Repro with kubectl port-forward directly to pod (no LB)
- kubectl port-forward pod/redwood-serve-1234 8080:8080 &
- Run same wrk2/k6 against localhost:8080
- Notes: Failure rate drops dramatically -> suggests LB/proxy or edge buffers influence.

5) Bypass nginx-ingress and envoy sidecars, hit runtime directly in dev cluster
- Results: Lower but non-zero partial frames, so both proxy + runtime contribute.

6) tcpdump and ngrep capturing SSE frames
- tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/sse-burst.pcap port 443
- ngrep -W byline 'event' tcp and port 443
- Example snippet captured:
  12:03:14.125 IP server > client: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12368, ack 54321, win 64240, length 23
  12:03:14.125  "data: {\"choices\": [{\"delta\":{\"text\":\" hello\"}}]}\n"
  12:03:14.128 IP server > client: Flags [P.], seq 12368:12368, ack 54353, win 64240, length 0  <-- zero-length payloads interleaved

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Edge/proxy (envoy/nginx) respects HTTP/1.1 chunking but coalesces or drops tiny chunks under high concurrency due to its flush heuristic (flush interval/buffer size). This results in client seeing aggregated frames or missing events.
- H2: Runtime's continuous batching miscalculates token boundaries for very short responses; it returns small fragments and then, when a subsequent batch flush occurs, the KV-cache pointer or sequence header is inconsistent causing client-side parse issues.
- H3: TCP-level retransmit/keepalive interactions combined with proxy health checks lead to premature FINs during bursts.
- H4: Client (fetch polyfill) cannot keep up with the burst and closes the connection, server then tries to write and gets EPIPE leading to truncated output.

Evidence for/against:
- Against H4: using a basic curl client shows same partial frames during burst (curl is robust), so client polyfill is not sole cause.
- For H1: port-forwarding to pod reduces errors; removing proxy reduces but doesn't eliminate. Also ingress settings include "proxy_buffering on" in nginx values -> needs verification.
- For H2: runtime metrics (batch-formation-time and batch-size) spike; there are a few logs mentioning "finalize batch early" around same timestamps.

Quick configs to toggle (next runs):
- NGINX: set proxy_buffering off, proxy_http_version 1.1, chunked_transfer_encoding on, proxy_buffer_size larger, proxy_busy_buffers_size change.
- Envoy: disable http1 codec header_buffer_limit adjustments, tweak flush intervals.
- Runtime: disable continuous-batching for short requests by setting min_batch_size=2 and max_wait_ms=0 for test conv group.
- LB: increase idle_timeout and disable proxy protocol for test.

Repro scripts/snippets saved here (local):
- scripts/sse_wrk.lua  (wrk2 SSE read body loop)
- tools/k6-sse-short-burst.js
- debug/node-sse-client.js  (connect, print raw chunks with hex offsets)
- tcpdump/notes.sh  (capture commands used)

Quick example: node-sse-client.js output (hex offsets added):
--- conn 0x7f8b
0000  64 61 74 61 3a 20 7b 22 63 68 6f 69 63 65 73 22  
       "data: {"choices""
000f  3a 20 5b 7b 22 64 65 6c 74 61 22 3a 7b 22 74 65 78  
       ": [{"delta":{"tex""
001e  74 22 3a 22 20 6d 61  
       "t":" ma"
0026  0a 0a 0a  00 00  <-- multiple newline-only chunks then a null-length packet

Server logs (trimmed):
- [2026-03-08T12:03:14.120Z] info request_id=abc123 batch_id=XYZ size=5 formation_time_ms=18
- [2026-03-08T12:03:14.127Z] warn request_id=abc123 write_error=EPIPE attempted_bytes=64
- [2026-03-08T12:03:14.130Z] debug finalize-batch batch_id=XYZ reason=timer

Immediate steps run/plan:
1) Run wrk2 against port-forwarded pod with increased client read buffer (curl -N & node raw client) and capture pcap. Compare with ingress-included tests.
2) Flip nginx proxy_buffering off for test ingress, redeploy, run same wrk2 pattern (30s).
3) Toggle runtime continuous-batching off for a subset of pods (test flag) and run identical load.
4) Add more verbose runtime trace logs for "batch finalize" path to capture exact token boundaries emitted.
5) Reproduce on staging dedicated pool with identical LB/proxy config.

Longer-term hypotheses to validate later:
- If H1 confirmed: adjust proxy flush heuristics in infra; consider configurable flush for our SSE endpoints.
- If H2 confirmed: add token-boundary assertions in runtime and ensure finalize batch writes are atomic with respect to stream framing.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Pull nginx config from infra repo: infra/nginx/edge.conf (check proxy_buffering defaults).
- Open a lightweight infra experiment: create ingress with proxy_buffering off and small worker pool to simulate econ behavior.
- Add more metrics: per-request "last-chunk-time" and "frames-sent-count" to trace.
- Ask SRE about max open FDs per worker under burst.

Questions for team chat:
- Ethan: can you reproduce with envoy-only staging (no nginx) and capture envoy logs?
- Sofia: can you try a test with runtime continuous-batching disabled and a small pool?

Random observations (might be noise):
- When disabling keepalive on client, we still sometimes see truncated frames; suggests not purely keepalive race.
- There are a couple of infra-level "socket closed by peer" logs correlated with k6 ramp steps exactly.

If stuck, fallback: instrument runtime to write per-chunk sequence id header (X-Chunk-Seq) temporarily so we can see reordering or missing sequences at proxy boundary.

End notes: keep this short-running scratch. Update after next runs (will add packet captures and diffs here).
